days.title: Rivers and Summits of the East
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: río Yeguas
stops.detail: Against this landscape of balance, the Yeguas River, a natural dividing line with the neighboring park, runs through its eastern slope across large gullies and carves out a steep valley of enormous beauty as it passes.

stops.name: Picos Colmena
stops.detail: The heights range between 180 and 828 m, and the highest points are located at Picos Colmena (828 m) and Pingajo (805 m).

stops.name: Cerro de la Minilla
stops.detail: Cerro de la Minilla: A place of transition between granite and carboniferous slates with gullied slopes.

stops.name: Ventorrillo de la Niña
stops.detail: Stratigraphic succession of Ventorrillo de la Niña: A slope formed by several ravines, where the sedimentary materials of the Park and their stratigraphic relationships can be observed.
